posts.title: Why Should I Learn Spanish Now That AI Exists?
posts.description: The Quandry I’m learning Spanish as an adult. Have you tried learning a new language? My previous few attempts were through school or university; but once classes ended, so did my literacy. This time, I’m trying something different: spaced repetition via the lovely apps Anki and Natulang. These systems sorta gameify learning through flashcards and daily practice, making it feel pleasurable. Snap-recalling the Spanish word for “pre-dawn” (la madrugada) is a very satisfying feeling. However, between these moments of blissful brain-etching, my pain-body interrupts with, “Whaddaya doin? Learnin language is a waste uh time once AI translators git good.” This thought is learning friction. It’s a new version of the classic “Why do I need to know math when calculators exist?”. This gets at the main reason people learn languages: to communicate. Of course, there are other valid and noble causes: cultural preservation, the joy of learning itself, Italian opera singing.
